checks.name: A13-api-surface
checks.summary: PASS. GET /v1/providers requires the owner role: 401 without authentication, 403 for the runner role, 200 for the owner. POST, PUT, DELETE and PATCH on the path all return 405, because the method check comes first: there is deliberately no reporting and no mutation verb here -- an observation rides on provider_observation of POST /v1/executions/result, an assignment rides on provider of POST /v1/executions/{execution_id}:start, and nothing on this surface can clear a runaway stop. CLOSED RESPONSE: the only top-level field is providers; each of the exactly three rows carries exactly the twelve named fields and every one of them is present (the schema puts all of them in required); runaway_detection carries exactly {scope, state, thresholds_declared_in} and concurrency exactly {active_assignments, declared_ceiling, ceiling_source, remaining, exhausted}; the row order is the fixed [codex claude opencode]. NO SYNTHETIC OR PLACEHOLDER VALUE and no field this Work Order did not name: the raw body is checked for TODO, placeholder, unknown-provider, example.com, '@', budget, quota, billing, spend, cost, credit, USD, usd, 16, 10.0 and 2.0 and contains none of them. With no observation at all every row reports health unknown, stale true and blocked_reason never-invoked-by-loop, authorized true with authorization_ref psa-foundation-001, and verified_by_loop_invocation false -- the surface reports what it knows and defaults to nothing reassuring. OPENAPI: contracts/openapi/openapi-v1.yaml gains the /v1/providers path (operationId listProviders, security iapOwner) and six schemas (ProviderObservation, ProviderAssignment, ProviderRunawayDetection, ProviderConcurrency, ProviderRegistryEntry, ProviderRegistryResponse), each with additionalProperties false and every field of the response schemas in required; StartRequest gains the optional provider and ResultRequest gains the optional provider_observation, both additive. The path is picked up by the same mechanical extraction internal/contracts uses (the ^  (/\S+):$ pattern now matches 24 paths, up from 23).

checks.name: A12-firestore-adapter-bounded-keyed-reads
checks.summary: Three new tests PASS against the local Firestore emulator, and the whole package is green with -race (26 top-level tests, up from 23, none skipped). TestProviderRegistryBehaviouralTableOnFirestore runs application.ProviderRegistryCases() by value -- the same 10 cases internal/application runs against the memory adapter -- and additionally asserts the side table really is keyed by Execution id on this adapter. TestProviderRegistryRollbackLeaksNothingOnFirestore asserts a failed transaction stages nothing and that the adapter itself refuses an undeclared Provider name and an observation with no observed instant, so no path can create a fourth registry document. MEASURED READ COUNT: TestProvidersReadCountDoesNotVaryWithRequirementCount builds a fixture at BOTH bounds for all three Providers (MaxProviderObservations = 32 observations and MaxProviderAssignments = 24 assignments each, with every assigned Execution present and non-terminal) and reads the adapter's own trued-up quota record before and after one GET /v1/providers. ONE GET /v1/providers READ 76 DOCUMENTS with 3 Requirements in the store and 76 with 11 -- identical, so the read count does not vary with the Requirement count -- against a declared bound of len(DeclaredProviders) * (1 + MaxProviderAssignments) + 1 = 76: one keyed registry document per declared Provider, one keyed Execution read per retained assignment, and the quota document. Nothing in that bound is a function of the Requirement count. A GET /v1/providers PERFORMS NO WRITE AND NO OUTBOX RECORD: measured writes = 1 in both runs, which is exactly the quota reservation every bounded owner read already writes. The quota reservation shape of no existing operation was changed. The adapter uses only the existing keyed read and write seams (unit.value and unit.stage), so no new record-envelope read site is introduced and firestore.indexes.json is untouched.
